layers.title: Chance a slope fails (factor of safety < 1)
layers.how_to_read: For each forecast day: share of 200 plausible soil-strength scenarios in which the slope is unstable, given forecast soil wetness. Steep, wet slopes turn orange/red. Soil parameters are assumed (literature ranges), so read it as relative danger, not a precise probability.

layers.title: Combined hazard: unstable slope x landslide trigger
layers.how_to_read: Slope-failure chance (physics) multiplied by how close the day's rain/soil conditions are to the landslide model's warning level. Dark red needs both a steep, weak slope and a wet trigger.

layers.title: Worst case: fully saturated soil
layers.how_to_read: P(FS<1) if the soil were completely saturated - where slopes would be most dangerous in an extreme monsoon.

layers.title: Slope angle
layers.how_to_read: Terrain steepness from the Copernicus DEM (30 m).

flood.note: Main-stem GloFAS cell chosen automatically (largest monsoon flow within 0.1 deg). GloFAS (~5 km) smooths steep Himalayan flash floods, so absolute peaks are underestimated; thresholds are relative to its own climatology.

validation.note: Calibration fitted only on training-period out-of-fold predictions (previously in-sample Platt, which under-predicted badly on unseen years). Gradient boosting reported as a comparison.

alert.disclaimer: Model-generated advisory for demonstration. Not an official warning; only authorised agencies (e.g. IMD, NDMA, USDMA) issue warnings.

inputs.name: River discharge
inputs.source: GloFAS v4 via Open-Meteo flood API

replay.note: Day-by-day replay using only models fitted on data up to 2012; river level from the calibrated model, flood level from the observed (reanalysis) discharge as a perfect-forecast upper bound; landslide targets from the NASA catalogue (to 2017-07) within ~60 km.

nisar_soil_moisture.note: NISAR SME2 (L3, provisional, 200 m EASE-Grid) median over the region vs ERA5-Land top layer (~9 km). Agreement in timing supports using ERA5-Land/forecast soil moisture as the slope-wetness forcing; NISAR observes the state on pass days.

validation.caveat: The GLC is compiled from news and reports: unreported landslides count as 'none', so probabilities are lower bounds and remote valleys are under-represented. Location accuracy 5-25 km; analysis cells are 0.5 deg (~50 km).

levels.name: GREEN
levels.label: Normal
levels.action: Conditions within the expected range. Continue routine monitoring.

levels.name: YELLOW
levels.label: Watch
levels.action: Conditions are changing. Increase monitoring; notify the monitoring team.

levels.name: ORANGE
levels.label: Warning
levels.action: Several indicators elevated. Verify on the ground; preparedness by responsible authorities.

levels.name: RED
levels.label: Critical
levels.action: Severe conditions. Escalate to authorities under an approved protocol (only they issue warnings).

assumptions: Soil cohesion 3-12 kPa (+5 kPa root cohesion under forest, +1.5 kPa under shrub/grass), friction angle 28-38 deg, soil depth 1-3 m (literature ranges for Himalayan colluvium). Slopes > 50 deg (bedrock cliffs), snow/ice and water are excluded.
Slope wetness from ERA5-Land / forecast soil moisture, rescaled between its 5th and 99th percentiles.

Landslide trigger: logistic model on rain/soil-moisture percentiles trained on 186 NASA Global Landslide Catalog events (2007-2012), isotonic calibration from leave-one-year-out predictions, tested on untouched 2013-2017 against the LHASA 7-day-rain rule; alert thresholds at the site's 90th/95th/99th percentile of model probability (1998-2017). Falls back to LHASA if the model is absent.

River model label: GloFAS discharge above the 2-year flood level within 3 days; trained on 1996-2012 with leave-one-year-out calibration, tested on untouched 2013-2019 (records after the 2020 GloFAS product break are excluded from training/testing; live alerts use post-break return levels).
Daily hazard probabilities are combined assuming independence between days.
